sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%无形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: There is a beauty to a universal standard.
sentences.zh: 通用标准具有一种美感。

sentences.en: The idea that people across the world can agree that when they interact with one specific thing,
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人们能够达成共识：当他们与某个特定事物互动时，

sentences.en: everyone will be on the same page.
sentences.zh: 所有人都能达成一致。

sentences.en: Regardless of language, or culture, or geographic locale.
sentences.zh: 无关语言、文化或地理位置。

sentences.en: If I'm in Belgrade, or Shanghai, or Sao Paulo,
sentences.zh: 如果我在贝尔格莱德、上海或圣保罗，

sentences.en: I can look at a sign and know instantly, without speaking a word of the local language,
sentences.zh: 我看到一个标志就能瞬间明白，无需说一句当地语言，

sentences.en: that this floor is slippery, that the emergency exit is over there,
sentences.zh: 这个地板很滑，紧急出口在那边，

sentences.en: and that that substance is poisonous, and I should not eat it.
sentences.zh: 那个物质是有毒的，我不应该吃它。

sentences.en: The group behind those internationally recognized logos is called ISO,
sentences.zh: 这些广受认可的标志背后的组织名为 ISO，

sentences.en: the International Organization for Standardization.
sentences.zh: 即国际标准化组织。

sentences.en: That's reporter Lauren Ober.
sentences.zh: 那是记者劳伦·奥伯。

sentences.en: And one of the most recognizable ISO symbols is the International Symbol of Access.
sentences.zh: 而最具辨识度的 ISO 符号之一就是国际无障碍符号。

sentences.en: That's the formal name of the blue and white logo with the stick figure in a wheelchair.
sentences.zh: 这是那个带有轮椅人形的蓝白标志的正式名称。

sentences.en: Around the world, you see the International Symbol of Access everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，你随处可见国际无障碍符号。

sentences.en: Parking spaces, on buttons that operate at automatic doors,
sentences.zh: 停车位、自动门的按钮上，

sentences.en: in bathrooms, and on seats on the bus or at movie theaters.
sentences.zh: 洗手间里，以及公交车或电影院的座位上。

sentences.en: Anywhere where there's an indication of special accommodations made for people with disabilities.
sentences.zh: 任何标明为残障人士提供特殊便利的地方。

sentences.en: Prior to the late 1960s, there was no universally agreed-upon accessibility icon.
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪 60 年代末之前，并没有一个普遍认可的无障碍图标。

sentences.en: Everyone used a different symbol, if they bothered to use one at all.
sentences.zh: 每个人都使用不同的符号，如果他们还会特意去用一个的话。

sentences.en: But in the 1960s, the disability rights movement started picking up steam.
sentences.zh: 但在 20 世纪 60 年代，残障人士权利运动开始积蓄力量。

sentences.en: In 1968, a group now called Rehabilitation International announced a design contest to create an international symbol of access.
sentences.zh: 1968 年，一个现名为“国际康复”的组织宣布了一场设计竞赛，旨在创造一个国际无障碍符号。

sentences.en: The logo would have to be readily identifiable from a reasonable distance, self-descriptive, simple, unambiguous, and practical.
sentences.zh: 该标志必须在合理距离内易于识别、具有自我说明性、简单、明确且实用。

sentences.en: The winner was a Danish designer named Susanna Kofool.
sentences.zh: 获胜者是一位名叫苏珊娜·科富尔的丹麦设计师。

sentences.en: The modern stick figure in wheelchair logo that we know today is actually a slightly modified version from the original.
sentences.zh: 我们今天所知的现代轮椅人形标志，实际上是原版的微调版本。

sentences.en: That one didn't have a head.
sentences.zh: 最初那个没有头。

sentences.en: Within a decade, the logo, the one with a head, was endorsed by both the United Nations and ISO.
sentences.zh: 不到十年时间，带有头部的这个标志便得到了联合国和 ISO 的认可。

sentences.en: Remember, this is the group that sets iconographic standards across countries.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是一个制定跨国图标标准的组织。

sentences.en: And so over time, this logo, the International Symbol of Access,
sentences.zh: 因此随着时间推移，这个标志——国际无障碍符号，

sentences.en: began to get embedded in the urban fabric of cities and towns across the world.
sentences.zh: 开始融入世界各地城镇的城市结构中。

sentences.en: People began to pay attention to the kinds of special building accommodations
sentences.zh: 人们开始关注各种特殊的建筑设施，

sentences.en: that spaces need to be inviting for people with varying degrees of ability.
sentences.zh: 这些空间需要具备这些设施，才能吸引不同行动能力的人。

sentences.en: And then in 1990, Congress passed the landmark Americans with Disabilities Act,
sentences.zh: 接着在 1990 年，国会通过了具有里程碑意义的《美国残疾人法案》，

sentences.en: which President George H.W.
sentences.zh: 由老乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush signed into law.
sentences.zh: 布什总统签署成为法律。

sentences.en: The ADA was modeled on the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
sentences.zh: 该法案是以 1964 年的《民权法案》为蓝本制定的。

sentences.en: The law, and I'm reading this from the ADA website here,
sentences.zh: 该法律——我在这里从 ADA 网站上宣读——

sentences.en: quote,
sentences.zh: 引述：

sentences.en: prohibits discrimination and guarantees that people with disabilities have the same opportunities
sentences.zh: 禁止歧视，并确保残障人士拥有与其他人相同的机会，

sentences.en: as everyone else to participate in the mainstream of American life,
sentences.zh: 参与美国生活的主流，

sentences.en: to enjoy employment opportunities,
sentences.zh: 享有就业机会，

sentences.en: to purchase goods and services,
sentences.zh: 购买商品和服务，

sentences.en: and to participate in state and local government programs and services,
sentences.zh: 以及参与州和地方政府的项目与服务，

sentences.en: end quote.
sentences.zh: 引述结束。

sentences.en: And I think it's fair to say that having a single attractive logo
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，拥有一个单一且吸引人的标志，

sentences.en: to signify a universal right for access helped create an atmosphere
sentences.zh: 来象征通用的无障碍权利，有助于创造这样一种氛围：

sentences.en: in which the built world could begin to adapt to new building parameters
sentences.zh: 在这个氛围中，人工建造的世界可以开始适应新的建筑参数

sentences.en: and regulations as specified per the ADA.
sentences.zh: 以及 ADA 规定的条例。

sentences.en: In many ways, the adoption of the international accessibility icon
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，国际无障碍图标的采用

sentences.en: is a success story in a simple design changing the world for the better.
sentences.zh: 是一个通过简单设计让世界变得更美好的成功故事。

sentences.en: I think the current image always has to be lauded for its historic importance.
sentences.zh: 我认为当前的形象因其历史重要性，永远都应该受到赞誉。

sentences.en: It's a form of wayfinding.
sentences.zh: 它是一种寻路方式。

sentences.en: It's a form of easy navigation in the environment.
sentences.zh: 它是环境中轻松导航的一种形式。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's historically profound.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，它具有深远的历史意义。

sentences.en: I mean, it's politically so important that now you know you're guaranteed
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它的政治意义如此重大，以至于现在你知道自己有了保障：

sentences.en: when you go out, you're going to find one of these spaces that's preserved.
sentences.zh: 当你出门时，你一定会找到这些被保留的空间之一。

sentences.en: You're able to count on accommodation.
sentences.zh: 你能够指望得到无障碍设施。

sentences.en: But this isn't the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是故事的全部。

sentences.en: Because as the logo got absorbed into the built environment,
sentences.zh: 因为随着这个标志被人工环境所吸收，

sentences.en: people with disabilities and their allies started finding it kind of lacking.
sentences.zh: 残障人士及其同盟开始发现它存在一些不足。

sentences.en: The shapes of the body and the body parts on that icon are squared off and geometric.
sentences.zh: 该图标上的身体和身体部位的形状是生硬的几何图形。

sentences.en: And even though it does have a head.
sentences.zh: 尽管它确实有一个头。

sentences.en: The head dangles from the neck and the neck is in this kind of unnaturally erect posture.
sentences.zh: 头部从脖子上垂下来，而脖子则呈这种很不自然的直立姿态。

sentences.en: There's not a sense of organic shapes of the body in space.
sentences.zh: 缺乏空间中身体有机形态的感觉。

sentences.en: That's Sarah Hendron, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，那是莎拉·亨德伦。

sentences.en: My name is Sarah Hendron.
sentences.zh: 我叫莎拉·亨德伦。

sentences.en: I'm an artist and design researcher in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 我是马萨诸塞州剑桥市的一名艺术家和设计研究员。

sentences.en: And I think a lot about prosthetics, adaptive technologies,
sentences.zh: 我经常思考假肢、自适应技术，

sentences.en: and disability studies and disability politics.
sentences.zh: 以及残疾研究和残疾政治。

sentences.en: Sarah Hendron is also a lecturer at RISD, the Rhode Island School of Design.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·亨德伦也是罗德岛设计学院（RISD）的讲师。

sentences.en: And most importantly for our purposes, Sarah is the co-founder of the Accessible Icon Project.
sentences.zh: 对我们而言最重要的是，莎拉是“无障碍图标项目”的联合创始人。

sentences.en: This movement, because that's what I think it has become, a movement,
sentences.zh: 这场运动——因为我认为它已经变成了一场运动——

sentences.en: is made up of designers, activists, artists, academics, and disability advocates
sentences.zh: 由设计师、活动家、艺术家、学者和残障倡导者组成，

sentences.en: all trying to change the conversation about disability in their communities.
sentences.zh: 他们都在努力改变其社区中关于残疾的对话。

sentences.en: And so for starters, the Accessible Icon Project has taken aim at the standard blue and white wheelchair icon.
sentences.zh: 因此首先，“无障碍图标项目”将矛头指向了标准的蓝白轮椅图标。

sentences.en: They've created a new icon that they hope will ultimately replace the ISO standard.
sentences.zh: 他们创造了一个新图标，希望最终能取代 ISO 标准。

sentences.en: It's still a white figure in a wheelchair positioned in a blue field,
sentences.zh: 它仍然是蓝色背景上的白色轮椅人形，

sentences.en: but the head and body are tilted forward.
sentences.zh: 但头部和身体向前倾斜。

sentences.en: The arm is angled back, as if it's propelling the user, and the wheel looks like it's in motion.
sentences.zh: 手臂向后倾斜，仿佛在推动使用者前进，且轮子看起来在运动中。

sentences.en: The visible leg is also moved forward and re-angled,
sentences.zh: 可见的那条腿也向前移动并重新调整了角度，

sentences.en: so it looks more active and doesn't just disappear into the wheel.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来更具活力，而不仅仅是消失在轮子里。

sentences.en: It looks modern, almost sleek.
sentences.zh: 它看起来很现代，甚至有些流线型。

sentences.en: You'll do a pretty good job picturing it if you imagine the new logo as the old logo, but italicized.
sentences.zh: 如果你把新标志想象成斜体版本的旧标志，就能很好地在脑海中勾勒出它的样子。

sentences.en: Changing an ISO standard isn't easy.
sentences.zh: 改变 ISO 标准并不容易。

sentences.en: A proposal has to be submitted and reviewed by ISO's Technical Committee on Graphical Symbols.
sentences.zh: 必须提交提案并由 ISO 图形符号技术委员会进行审查。

sentences.en: Then it has to be considered by symbols experts from around the world,
sentences.zh: 然后必须由来自世界各地的符号专家进行审议，

sentences.en: and then finally approved by ISO's member countries.
sentences.zh: 最后由 ISO 成员国批准。

sentences.en: I talked with Barry Gray, the chairman of the Technical Committee on Graphical Symbols.
sentences.zh: 我采访了图形符号技术委员会主席巴里·格雷。

sentences.en: Oh my god, I want Barry Gray's job.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我好想做巴里·格雷的工作。

sentences.en: He says he's seen the new logo and applauds the designers for the icon's dynamism.
sentences.zh: 他说他看过新标志，并赞赏设计师赋予图标的动态感。

sentences.en: But, he told me, a lot of factors would have to be taken into account
sentences.zh: 但是，他告诉我，在替换当前符号之前必须考虑很多因素，

sentences.en: before the current symbol could be replaced.
sentences.zh: 比如这个新图标是否会被误认为用于轮椅竞速的符号。

sentences.en: Like whether this new icon might be confused with symbols used for wheelchair racing.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管当前标志做了很多好事，莎拉·亨德伦等人

sentences.en: So, as much good as the current logo has done, Sarah Hendren, among others,
sentences.zh: 对该标志描绘残障人士的方式提出了异议。

sentences.en: takes issue with how the logo portrays people with disabilities.
sentences.zh: 它有一种不动的感觉。

sentences.en: It has this immobile look to it.
sentences.zh: 图像中的人物看起来像是在等待被人推着走。

sentences.en: The figure in the image looks like it's waiting to be pushed around.
sentences.zh: 并不是说以这种方式体验移动能力的任何人有什么不对。

sentences.en: It's not that there's anything wrong with anyone who experiences mobility in that way.
sentences.zh: 只是对亨德伦而言，该图标传达的隐含信息是

sentences.en: It's just that for Hendren, the implicit message the icon sends
sentences.zh: 残障人士是无助的。

sentences.en: is that people with disabilities are helpless.
sentences.zh: 而这个新标志赋予了轮椅上的人物一种自主感。

sentences.en: And this new logo grants a sense of autonomy to the figure in the wheelchair.
sentences.zh: 并且人从哪里开始、椅子从哪里开始，有了更清晰的划分。

sentences.en: And there's a clearer delineation between where the person starts and the chair begins.
sentences.zh: 我认为前一个图标所缺少的是，它没有任何向前移动的定义。

sentences.en: I think what the former icon lacked was there just wasn't any definition of moving forward.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它有点太刻板了。

sentences.en: You know, it was just kind of stoic.
sentences.zh: 而这个符号表明马尔登社区正全速前进。

sentences.en: Whereas this symbol shows that the Malden community is moving full steam ahead.
sentences.zh: 我们都在全速前进。

sentences.en: We are all moving full steam ahead.
sentences.zh: 加里·克里斯滕森是马萨诸塞州马尔登的市长，这是一个拥有约 6 万人口的城镇。

sentences.en: Gary Christensen is the mayor of Malden, Massachusetts, a town of about 60,000.
sentences.zh: 6 万名多元化的居民。

sentences.en: 60,000 diverse residents.
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕森市长与一个名为“三角形”的残障倡导组织合作，

sentences.en: Mayor Christensen worked with a disability advocacy organization called Triangle
sentences.zh: 用以替换马尔登各处的旧符号。

sentences.en: to replace the old symbol all over Malden.
sentences.zh: 他对此充满热情。

sentences.en: And he is really enthusiastic about it.
sentences.zh: 他希望……

sentences.en: He wants...
sentences.zh: 尽快让马尔登这里每一个能想到的地方都换上这个无障碍图标项目。

sentences.en: To have every conceivable spot here in Malden replaced with this accessible icon project as soon as possible.
sentences.zh: 如果你跟“三角形”的杰夫·金特里谈谈，

sentences.en: If you talk to Jeff Gentry from Triangle,
sentences.zh: 他会告诉你我给他发过邮件、打过电话、发过短信、甚至用信鸽传过信，

sentences.en: he would tell you that I've emailed him, called him, texted him, pigeon carried him
sentences.zh: 只为弄清楚我们什么时候才能换掉马尔登市这里的每一个符号。

sentences.en: to find out when we can replace every symbol here in the city of Malden.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想要努力实现这一绝佳倡议的急切心情。

sentences.en: That's how eager I am to try and fulfill this wonderful initiative.
sentences.zh: 在我们对话的这个时刻，市长把电话交给了“三角形”的杰夫·金特里。

sentences.en: At this point in our conversation, the mayor handed the phone over to Jeff Gentry from Triangle.
sentences.zh: 嗨，劳伦。

sentences.en: Hi, Lauren.
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: “三角形”和市长办公室共同将新标志引入了马尔登的塔尔博茨配送中心

sentences.en: Together, Triangle and the mayor's office have gotten the new logo at the Talbots Distribution Center in Malden
sentences.zh: 以及克拉克鞋业，该公司将其美国

sentences.en: and at Clark's Shoes, which has its U.S.
sentences.zh: 总部设在不远处的马萨诸塞州牛顿市。

sentences.en: headquarters in Newton, Mass., not too far away.
sentences.zh: 残障人士不再接受分离但平等的对工作、学校和生活机会。

sentences.en: People with disabilities are no longer accepting separate but equal work, school, and life opportunities.
sentences.zh: 他们正朝着更丰富的未来迈进。

sentences.en: They're moving forward towards a richer future.
sentences.zh: 希望这个图标能围绕这一点引发对话。

sentences.en: And hopefully the icon creates dialogue around that.
sentences.zh: 我相信无障碍图标正在创造一个更具包容性的世界，就像我们在这里的马尔登所建设的那样。

sentences.en: And I believe that the accessible icon is creating a more inclusive world like we're building here in Malden.
sentences.zh: 当我询问支持新标牌的倡导者他们是如何扩大其使用范围时，

sentences.en: When I asked pro-new signage advocates about how they're expanding its use,
sentences.zh: 他们会指出其他地方的本地成功案例。

sentences.en: they would point to local success stories elsewhere.
sentences.zh: “三角形”的杰夫·金特里和无障碍图标项目的莎拉·亨德伦都向我推荐了一个人，

sentences.en: Both Jeff Gentry and Sarah Hendren from the Accessible Icon Project referred me to a guy named
sentences.zh: 我叫布伦丹·希尔德雷斯。

sentences.en: My name is Brendan Hildreth.
sentences.zh: 布伦丹·希尔德雷斯，北卡罗来纳州的残障权利活动家。

sentences.en: Brendan Hildreth, a disability rights activist in North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 你好，我叫布伦丹。

sentences.en: Hello, my name is Brendan.
sentences.zh: 我不是机器或机器人。

sentences.en: I am not a machine or robot.
sentences.zh: 布伦丹患有脑瘫和听力损失，通过增强型沟通设备或发声机器说话。

sentences.en: Brendan has cerebral palsy and hearing loss and speaks through an augmentative communication device or a talking machine.
sentences.zh: 我们这里使用的是采访文字记录来重现它。

sentences.en: We reproduced it here using an interview transcript.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这个项目远不止是一张图片和一个符号。

sentences.en: This project is way more than just a picture and a symbol to me.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这个项目表明残障人士可以保持活跃并参与其中。

sentences.en: The project to me shows that people with disabilities can be active and participate.
sentences.zh: 它让人们了解残障权利运动。

sentences.en: It makes people understand about the disabilities rights movement.
sentences.zh: 布伦丹一直致力于将无障碍标志引入他的小镇新伯尔尼。

sentences.en: Brendan has been working to bring the accessibility sign to his town, New Bern.
sentences.zh: 我与当地的电视台和广播电台就新图标进行了很多交谈。

sentences.en: I did a lot speaking with television and radio stations locally about the new icon.
sentences.zh: 我有一封来自州的信件，允许我在这里使用该图标。

sentences.en: I have a letter from the state to allow me to use the icon here.
sentences.zh: 我已经在新伯尔尼的几家企业画了新图标，还有很多要做。

sentences.en: I have painted the new icon in several businesses in New Bern and still have many more to do.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州州级层面的人很喜欢这个新图标。

sentences.en: People at the North Carolina state level like the new icon.
sentences.zh: 他们感谢我把这个图标带到这里。

sentences.en: They thanked me for bringing the icon here.
sentences.zh: 杰夫、布莱恩和莎拉。

sentences.en: Jeff, Brian, and Sarah.
sentences.zh: 也就是“三角形”的杰夫·金特里，以及无障碍图标项目的布莱恩·格利尼和莎拉·亨德伦。

sentences.en: As in Jeff Gentry of Triangle and Brian Glennie and Sarah Hendren from the Accessible Icon Project.
sentences.zh: 意识到有多少企业正在采用我带来的新图标。

sentences.en: Realized how many businesses I am getting to use the new icon.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·亨德伦表示，她对她所谓的“标牌洗绿”不感兴趣，也就是为了政治正确而更换标志。

sentences.en: Sarah Hendren says she's not interested in what she calls sign washing or getting the logo changed just to be politically correct.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·亨德伦表示，她对她所谓的“招牌粉饰”或仅仅为了政治正确而更改徽标不感兴趣。

sentences.en: She says this project is a process of consciousness raising, quote unquote, so that each time the sign is officially changed,
sentences.zh: 她说这个项目是一个所谓的“提高意识”的过程，因此每当标志被正式更换时，

sentences.en: there's intention around it and dialogue about disability.
sentences.zh: 其中就会包含有关的意图以及关于残障的对话。

sentences.en: But a symbol meant to start dialogue and spread through grassroots action is very different than one created to be a universal and internationally recognized symbol.
sentences.zh: 但是，一个旨在引发对话并通过基层行动传播的标志，与一个旨在成为通用且国际认可的标志的标志有着很大的不同。

sentences.en: There's a lack of clarity as to whether this new sign meets the standards put into effect by the Americans with Disabilities Act.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚这个新标志是否符合《美国残疾人法案》所实施的标准。

sentences.en: Even though the law states that reasonable changes can be made to this symbol as long as it clearly displays the wheelchair and indicates accessibility,
sentences.zh: 尽管法律规定，只要该标志清晰展示轮椅并标明无障碍设施，就可以对其进行合理更改，

sentences.en: there are still questions about what constitutes a functional equivalent.
sentences.zh: 但对于什么才构成功能上的等同，仍然存在疑问。

sentences.en: New York City had planned to adopt the new logo in all five boroughs, but this legal ambiguity caused them to hold off implementing it, at least for now.
sentences.zh: 纽约市曾计划在所有五个行政区采用新标志，但这种法律上的模糊性导致他们暂缓推行，至少目前如此。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people end up buying that old original image because they're nervous about complying with ADA code.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多人最终还是购买那个古老的原始图像，因为他们担心无法合规于《美国残疾人法案》的准则。

sentences.en: And I think what we're trying to do is say, look, functional equivalence has a kind of legal set of definitions and contours.
sentences.zh: 我想我们试图表达的是，看吧，功能等同有着一套法律上的定义和轮廓。

sentences.en: Those are the things that are going to probably need to be worked out at the state level.
sentences.zh: 这些可能是需要在州层面去解决的问题。

sentences.en: But it's not as though functional equivalence means willy-nilly personal interpretation.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着功能等同就等同于随心所欲的个人解读。

sentences.en: It means as long as it's perfectly clear that you're indicating access for wheelchair users, you can do a different kind of version of the icon.
sentences.zh: 这意味着只要能非常清楚地表明你在为轮椅使用者指引无障碍通道，你就可以使用不同版本的图标。

sentences.en: So it all comes back to the question of what we are trying to accomplish through our symbols.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切又回到了我们试图通过符号来实现什么目标的问题上。

sentences.en: Having one unified icon can tell one clear story all over the world.
sentences.zh: 拥有一个统一的图标可以在全世界讲述一个清晰的故事。

sentences.en: But sometimes stories change.
sentences.zh: 但有时故事会发生变化。

sentences.en: We said earlier that the group behind the original call for an international symbol of access is called Rehabilitation International.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才说过，最初呼吁建立国际无障碍符号的那个组织叫做“国际康复组织”。

sentences.en: Well, in the 1940s, it was known by another name, the International Society for the Welfare of Cripples.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在20世纪40年代，它曾被称为另一个名字：国际残疾人福利协会。

sentences.en: The meanings and associations that words have shift over time.
sentences.zh: 词语所具有的含义和联想会随着时间而改变。

sentences.en: And sometimes the symbols need to as well.
sentences.zh: 有时符号也需要随之改变。

sentences.en: But you know, universality, it does have an upside, especially if you're in Belgrade and you're about to accidentally eat poison.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，通用性确实有它的好处，特别是如果你在贝尔格莱德而且正要不小心吃下毒药的话。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Lauren Ober with Sam Greenspan, Avery Truffelman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由劳伦·奥伯与萨姆·格林斯潘、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼以及我罗曼·马尔斯共同制作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Pike Malinovsky, who helped with, among other things, pronouncing designer Susanna Kufoul's name.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢派克·马利诺夫斯基，他在诸如正确发音设计师苏珊娜·库福尔的名字等方面提供了帮助。

sentences.en: So here comes a pronouncer for Susanna Kufoul.
sentences.zh: 接下来是苏珊娜·库福尔的读音示范。

sentences.en: Which, I'd like to point out, is spelled K-O-E-F-O-E-D?
sentences.zh: 顺便指出，它的拼写是 K-O-E-F-O-E-D？

sentences.en: Kufoul.
sentences.zh: 库福尔。

sentences.en: Let me say that again.
sentences.zh: 让我再说一遍。

sentences.en: Susanna Kufoul.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜·库福尔。

sentences.en: I do not hear the D in Kufoul.
sentences.zh: 我没有在库福尔里听到D的音。

sentences.en: Kufoul.
sentences.zh: 库福尔。

sentences.en: Kufoul.
sentences.zh: 库福尔。

sentences.en: Susanna Kufoul.
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜·库福尔。

sentences.en: I still don't know.
sentences.zh: 我还是搞不懂。

sentences.en: That doesn't make sense to me at all.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说完全说不通。

sentences.en: That's how you say that.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的读音。

sentences.en: But then again, that's Danish for you.
sentences.zh: 不过话又说回来，这就是丹麦语的特色。

sentences.en: Cheers.
sentences.zh: 干杯。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio KALW in San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign, an architecture firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 本地公共广播电台 KALW 的一个节目，在美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心的建筑事务所 ArcSign 的办公室里制作。

sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并给这个节目点赞。

sentences.zh: 我的推特账号是 Roman Mars。

sentences.en: Sam tweets at Sam Listens.
sentences.zh: 萨姆的推特账号是 Sam Listens。

sentences.en: Avery tweets at Truffelman.
sentences.zh: 艾弗里的推特账号是 Truffelman。

sentences.en: Oh, Avery also runs our Tumblr, which is at 99percentinvisible.tumblr.com, which you'll really like.
sentences.zh: 哦，艾弗里还负责我们的 Tumblr，网址是 99percentinvisible.tumblr.com，你一定会喜欢它的。

sentences.en: You should check it out.
sentences.zh: 你应该去看看。

sentences.en: But if you want to do us a real solid this week, go to 99pi.org, search for your favorite episode of 99% Invisible, and then tweet and Facebook that sucker.
sentences.zh: 但如果你这周想帮我们一个大忙，请访问 99pi.org，搜索你最喜欢的《99%隐形》单集，然后把那个宝贝转到推特和 Facebook 上。

sentences.zh: 分享就是关爱，尽在 99pi.org。
